title: Owned durable existing-file publication receipt
description: Problem: generated existing files need durable owner-safe delivery without exposing workspace paths. Decision: immutable artifact text codec; UTF-8 documents retain their format, binary attachments use a canonical base64 envelope physically stored as markdown and presented as file. Alternatives rejected: caller-controlled path serving, public static hosting, DB format migration. Only explicit publication with verified task roots and an owned existing conversation is authorized. Images remain separate.

x-policy.cancellation: Optional host cancelled callable checked before open, per read chunk, after snapshot validation and immediately before artifact.create; raises InterruptedError with no publication event. Once artifact.create commits, caller must settle its existing task lifecycle rather than erase durable bytes.
x-policy.fileRead: Absolute verified roots only; no-follow every root/path component; reject traversal, symlink, special file, changed inode/size/mtime/ctime or renamed path; complete cancellable read. Documents strict UTF-8, no replacement decoding. No external resource fetching or bundling.
x-policy.dedupe: Same conversation/content reuses only compatible source, owner, format, MIME, digest and envelope provenance; collision refuses without modifying existing evidence. First published filename/title remains stable.
x-policy.delivery: All HTTP artifact reads and lifecycle access require authenticated conversation owner, including legacy sources; missing/deleted conversations deny. No path-serving endpoint. Raw/view and metadata-content never expose binary envelopes. Downloads attachment, nosniff, private no-store. HTML/SVG default download retains bytes but uses inert text/plain and .txt suffix; interactive=1 is explicit original download with warning. Raw sandbox disallows scripts; existing panel script opt-in remains separate. Response-file HTML/SVG PDF export is refused until the legacy browser renderer has a complete inert execution boundary; Markdown export remains available.
x-policy.events: Caller emits existing artifact lifecycle event using receipt.artifact, task_id and artifact UUID. No second persistence or event system.
